after: ## Turning a broad topic into issues
alt: A rejected statement, War causes suffering, is not an issue because almost nobody disagrees. Three usable issues follow: globally, weapons sales to governments in conflict; nationally, trials or a truth commission after civil conflict; locally, neighbours settling disputes without the police.
caption: An issue is a question that people answer differently.

after: ## Turning a broad topic into issues
alt: Five stepped cards running from short-term to long-term: ceasefire, peacemaking, peacekeeping, peacebuilding and reconciliation, each with its definition, beside an arrow from stopping the fighting to fixing the causes. Mediation is defined below as a neutral third person helping the sides reach their own agreement.
caption: Stopping the fighting and fixing the causes are different jobs with different names.

after: ## Perspectives and why people hold them
alt: Four perspectives on compulsory national service. Leaning for: a defence ministry (readiness and unity, because its job is security) and an employer (discipline and teamwork, because it gains skilled workers). Leaning against: a young person (delays study and work) and a peace group (normalises violence). The ministry and employer may have a vested interest.
caption: For each perspective, ask who holds it, what they argue and why their position leads them there.

alt: Five possible causes (scarce resources, unequal treatment, historical grievances, political exclusion, misinformation) feed into conflict, which leads to five possible consequences (displacement, interrupted schooling, damage, lasting distrust, and sometimes new laws or cooperation). Below, a chain: a grazing land dispute leads farmers and herders to avoid the shared market, trade falls, and a reason to keep the peace is lost.
caption: Causes of conflict are often disputed; link them to consequences in chains rather than lists.

alt: Indicators grouped into three areas (societal safety and security, ongoing conflict, militarisation) combine into one Global Peace Index ranking. Its strength is a consistent method across many countries; it hides choices about which indicators to include, how to weight them and how reliable data are where reporting is difficult.
caption: A single number is only as good as the choices behind it.

after: ## Courses of action and their effects
alt: A table of five actions with a strength and a limitation each: the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty, UN peacekeeping, the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission and school peer mediation. Below, five criteria for assessing any action.
caption: Every real action has a limitation; judge each one against the same criteria.

alt: A fictional charity claims trust rose sharply after its dialogue programme. Four tagged steps evaluate it: the charity’s own survey supports it; the charity has a vested interest; the organisers ran the survey; so an independent body should repeat it, including non-attenders.
caption: End an evaluation by suggesting how the claim could be tested.
